utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon all. Your Honours, before I proceed I should like to raise a question briefly. And at the -- I want to do that at the very outset in order to allow for checking. As I have no contact with the client, there is something that I thought I observed yesterday in connection with his health, so if it is possible I should like to tell you about it in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. We shall go into closed session or private session, rather.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, we had hoped that we would be able to sit for longer hours next week each day; however, in view of what you've said we shall abandon the plan to try and arrange that next week but will continue to look for other opportunities. As far as tomorrow is concerned, it seems to us that Mr. Lazarevic himself has offered the solution which is that if he should feel unwell, he should draw that to the attention of the Bench and we will deal with it as it and if it arises. Otherwise, we shall proceed on the same schedule as we had planned, which was to try to sit for five hours tomorrow. So please continue now with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, yesterday prior to the adjournment we spoke about how the Pristina Corps command was taking measures for stepping up combat-readiness. At this point I should like you to tell us what was the possibility of manning the Pristina Corps with military conscripts from the territory of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the recruitment plan for the Pristina Corps, with conscripts belonging to the reserve ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry for interrupting you, Mr. Lazarevic. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The recruitment plan for manning war units of the Pristina Corps with military conscripts of the reserve force envisaged that from the territory of Kosovo and Metohija the recruitment should be carried out with about 11.000 conscripts and from outside the Kosovo territory to engage about 14.000 military conscripts; namely, this indicates that there was not enough possibilities to man the corps from the basic zone -- actually, it could only provide under 50 per cent of the required number. And the superior command proceeded in a planned fashion to man the Pristina Corps on the basis of what was referred to as the ex-territorial principle.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. At the level of the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army, did there exist a plan for the defence of the country?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. These were special plans to be used by the Yugoslav Army at a certain point in the past used to be called war plans. And concretely speaking about the engagement of the 3rd Army and the Pristina Corps for the relevant period, 1999, the basis of that plan was the Grom 3 plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for the transcript this plan is Exhibit 3D690. Can we have Exhibit 3D696 brought up in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, can you recognise this document and can you comment on it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know this document. I know about it from this trial, but what is ordered in the document is something that I'm familiar with from the time prior to the war, about the 10th of March, when the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army ordered the 2nd Army and sent this to the 3rd Army for their information to organize concerted action between these two armies, specifically between the 2nd Army and its Podgorica Corps and the Pristina Corps, with a view to closing off routes between Montenegro and Kosovo and Metohija via the Rugova gorge where there was a heightened spillover of heavy terrorist forces. The Chief of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia, General Ojdanic, ordered that the concerted action plan should be realised and specifically says in item 2 that the command of the Pristina Corps should participate in that task. That order is from about the 10th of March, it is not quite legible here in the heading, the year being 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Here in item 2 they refer to the plan of coordination. Is that what we referred to yesterday when we said plan of coordination or concerted action when you say that one had not been prepared?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are quite right. For the army units that were not in a mutual system of subordination and superiority, a plan of mutual coordination is prepared in terms of tasks, objectives, place, and time, and normally the superior command to both -- orders to both structures, issues orders to both structures, and gives them the basics, the fundaments, of the plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, what's the relationship between the document on the screen and Grom 3?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Grom 3 as a special-purpose plan at the level of the Yugoslav Army from the level of the General Staff down to brigade level within the framework of the Pristina Corps and the 3rd Army partly referred also to the air force and the anti-aircraft defence and the 2nd Army, not the entire Yugoslav Army, that is. And it implies the defence of the country's integrity against attacks by the multi-national brigade of the NATO forces from Macedonia with the simultaneous armed rebellion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I understand all that. What's the relationship between that plan and this document, if any?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do want to confirm that there is a relationship because this corridor was observed between Kosovo and Metohija and Montenegro and on towards Albania, a corridor for the introduction of heavy terrorist forces from Albania. The General Staff observed that and the chief ordered that these two structures, the 2nd Army and the 3rd Army, are -- either Pristina Corps and the Podgorica Corps should seal off that route in coordinated action. This is a concretization in practice part of the Grom plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, we're still on this topic and I should like to ask you: How was the use of the units of the Pristina Corps plan at the level of the 3rd Army, was there any order, command, or plan in that connection as well?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may be sufficiently precise, Grom 3 at the level of the General Staff ended around the 16th of January, 1999, and according to a certain methodology and procedure, the 3rd Army drew up its own plan for the defence of the integrity of the country - this was Grom 3 - but for the 3rd Army, around the 27th, that is ten days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, let's see that document in e-court and then we can comment on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I see 5D245, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, is this the plan for the engagement of the Pristina Corps issued by the command of the 3rd Army?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be more precise here, this is an order issued by the 3rd Army command on the 27th of January, 1999, it's a state secret, it's part of the Grom 3 plan and it's an order for the use not only of the Pristina Corps but of the 3rd Army in preventing the forceful introduction of a NATO brigade, its routing, and the destruction of the forces of the armed rebellion. To be completely precise, the Grom 3 plan contained apart from this central order which was the fundamental document, a large number of other documents as well, but this is the basic and fundamental document for the Grom 3 plan at the level of the 3rd Army. And within the scope of this order, the place, role, and tasks of the Pristina Corps are determined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can we see the end of that document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we will come to the end. It's a document consisting of more than one page. I will ask the General to comment on an item in the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, let's take a look at item 5 where tasks are assigned to the units and can you comment on that, please. It's on page 5, it's page 5 and item 5, and then there's 5.1, the Pristina Corps. Can you see item 5, General, and can you comment on it, please? Are these tasks for the units of the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the directive of the Chief of the General Staff, the 3rd Army commander issued orders to all the units under him, and in item 5.1 to the Pristina Corps as follows: In the first phase engage the regular forces and armed non-Siptar population in Kosovo and Metohija with reinforcements, and these are three combat groups listed here, with anti-aircraft defence measures, continue strengthening the depth security of the state border and prevent an attack by a multi-national brigade of NATO from Macedonia, secure roads, block terrorist and sabotage strongholds in Kosovo and Metohija, and prevent their linking up with NATO. He stated that the armed non-Siptar population should be used only for certain purposes, to secure military facilities and roads and to defend populated, built-up areas. That's the first stage. The second stage with stronger reinforcements for the Pristina Corps consisting of several brigades and with mobilisation carried out, neutralise the NATO forces should they penetrate deeper into the territory of Kosovo and Metohija and suppress the armed rebellion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, could you clarify a point, please. We'll soon come to the order issued by you, we'll see that later, and the armed non-Siptar population is mentioned there also. Can you tell us how you understood this order, and we shall see later on whether any tasks were assigned and so on.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my assessment, both then and now, the 3rd Army commander relied in doctrinal terms on the rules of combat and the instructions for combat and also on the Law on Defence, according to which apart from the army on the territory of Kosovo and Metohija other forces can be engaged and these are forces of the Ministry of Defence, the civilian protection, and civil defence. And in my orders I respected this, I complied with the order I received, but also as the corps commander within the scope of what was permitted by the instructions, I gave slightly different tasks to the brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We'll come back to that, General, but for now I'd like you to tell me, if you know, whether the Albanian population agreed, whether it wanted to enter the civil defence. Because here it says the armed non-Siptar population. You explained now what this referred to, but I would like to know whether while you were down there they wanted to take part.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, apart from isolated cases - and now I'm referring to the Albanian population in particular but also other non-Siptar inhabitants of Kosovo and Metohija, those belonging to the Turkish, Muslim, Gorani, and Roma ethnic communities - participated in the defence of the country.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, you ground your answer in the rules of combat and the Law on Defence. Do these documents use the expression "armed non-Siptar population"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that term is not used, as is stated here, but the term "population" and engagement of the population in armed struggle and other non-armed forms of resistance is used and is provided for, both in the Law on Defence and the rules of combat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Have I misunderstood you as stating that these are identifiable groups called civil defence and civil protection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Law on Defence provides for the following: Citizens, as defined in the Law on Defence, whereas in the rules of combat they're defined as the population, but I am going back to the Law on Defence. Citizens may be organized, armed, and included in the defence of the country within the scope of the Ministry of Defence, and they can be sent to units of civilian defence and -- civil defence and civilian protection. And that's what I was referring to a little while ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we'll come to that also and we will have exhibits, and then we can further clarify if need be as regards the civil defence and the civilian protection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, please be kind enough -- so kind as to comment on item 11, that's on page 12, the last page, because His Honour did want to see the last page. Item 11, as regards command, what was envisaged here? Who was to be in command according to this order?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In item 11, command and communications, what is stated is the following: The army command with its command post in Nis and forward command post in Pristina, the Kosovski Junaci barracks will be in command. I want to say that the forward command post on the 2nd of February had already been set up in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: After issuing this order or after this order was issued, did the 3rd Army command issue any further orders in order to prevent surprises and maintain the level of combat-readiness according to this order?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to the same principle, just as the Chief of the General Staff issued other orders also, the 3rd Army command monitored the situation. And apart from this fundamental special-purpose plan it issued a number of specific orders for specific tasks, making operational this plan we are now talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have in e-court 5D249 --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: For you to comment on. Do you recognise this document? It's a document of the 3rd Army command addressed to the Pristina Corps and other units. Please can you comment on this document.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order issued by the commander of the 3rd Army, General Pavkovic, only a few days after this initial order from the Grom 3 plan, that is, the 1st of February. And he orders the taking of measures to prevent surprises in the area of the 3rd Army, focusing on the area of the Pristina Corps, because there was a high concentration of NATO forces in the Adriatic Sea and the Mediterranean.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sorry for interrupting you.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He explains in the preamble what can be expected from these forces, and then in item 1 he orders that dispersion of military assets should immediately begin, dispersion from warehouses and depots.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can we now move on and comment on item 3, which is on page 2 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see page 2, item 3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With a view to preventing insupportable losses from the first air-strikes, the army commander ordered that fortification of the units should immediately continue in the second degree of protection; he's referring to the forces along the state border towards Macedonia and Albania in the system of securing and defending the state border.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: To avoid confusion we see an abbreviation here at the end where it says SAJ, what does SAJ mean responsible corps and SAJ commands?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the ones responsible are the command of the Pristina Corps and independent army units. The engineers regiment, and this has to do with obstacle, the construction of obstacles.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Please look at items 4 and 5, please.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is now something that makes more specific the general plan, Grom 3, and the army commander here is ordering at the corps level that a plan be drafted for the defence of the border and the closing of axes along which terrorist forces might be infiltrated. And now we see that the army commander is no longer referring to securing the state border, although it's early February, but the defence of the state border. He's ordering that this plan be drafted within 15 days. The deadline is the 15th of February, 1999. In item 5 he orders that at the level of the Pristina Corps command a special plan be drafted for blocking and destroying the forces of the armed rebellion in the Drenica, Lab, and Malisevo sectors in coordination with units of the MUP. These are four operational KLA zones where there was the highest concentration of those forces. They had 8 to 10.000 [Realtime transcript read in error "eight to ten members"] members there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General -- I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, can you help us by identifying what particular issue all this detailed evidence goes to that you feel makes it necessary to go through it bit by bit in this way orally in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I want to show you now - and you will see later on from these plans - we will come to the plans and the orders of the Joint Command quite soon, or rather, those that bear the heading the Joint Command so that you might be able to understand those orders and also to see how the chain and the system of command functioned regarding all those important issues. We felt that it would be necessary for you to look at the whole process, how plans were transferred from one level to another in the chain of command. And we will try to give you an explanation about the orders that have been tendered by the Prosecution, but I think they can be used in order to be able to understand this whole issue of the Joint Command, how the chain of planning and ordering functioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. That makes it much easier now to follow when it's clear what the objective is at the end, and therefore you should continue as you think appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, sir, there is an error in the transcript page 12, line 24, it says in the transcript eight to ten members and it should read 8 to 10.000 members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said four operative zones --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We have the problem we had yesterday of not speaking into the microphone. You seem locate yourself where there isn't a microphone -- perhaps in the second and third sessions today you would sit in the seat to your left if that's possible so that you're speaking into a high microphone. There's a difference in height, you'll see, in these microphones, and if you were sitting further to your left you would be speaking into that. Even if you move your lectern a little just now, it will probably make a difference. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, do I have to repeat the question or were you able to understand what I was asking you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understood you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But -- I'm sorry. Yes, but I hear now that the interpreters were not able to hear the question. At any rate, you said that this was a plan for the destruction of the terrorists in four operational zones, and we see here that it says Drenica, Lab, and Malisevo. Can you please clarify that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is not a mistake. These are three areas where there was a major build-up of forces, and four operational zones of the KLA were situated there and they had 8 to 10.000 members. Three areas, four operational zones within those three areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. I just wanted to make that clear. Could you please look at paragraph 12 and comment on it, that's page 3 in this document.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In item 12 the commander of the 3rd Army orders that preparations be carried out for a rapid call-up and reporting of personnel from the reserve with certain important critical specialties, primarily to be recruited into the anti-aircraft artillery and rocket units. So this is a preparatory task.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, let us move on now to the planning of the use at level of the Pristina Corps command. So what was the sequence of the orders at those later stages? Perhaps it would be easier if we could have a Prosecution exhibit, P2808 up on our screens, and then you can comment on it.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked me about the sequence for the planning process. It was the sequence that was envisaged in the decision and the order of the 3rd Army commander. In the Pristina Corps on the 7th of February, a full Grom 3 plan was drafted for all the corps units, and what we see here on our screens is the implementation of the task from a previous order of the 3rd Army commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: That was supposed to be completed by the 15th -- General, could you please wait for me to finish the question and for the interpretation to finish.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a special order dated the 1st of February, 1999, the 3rd Army commander ordered that plans be drafted in the corps, that a plan be drafted, for the destruction and routing of terrorist forces in the area of Malo Kosovo, Drenica, and Malisevo. Acting in accordance with this item in that order, the corps command did draft its own order and a larger number of documents that were appended to the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, could you please look at paragraph 1, the enemy. I think that here we have the answer to my question about the four operational zones. Could you please just comment on paragraph 1 and then we will move on.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In paragraph 1 of this order, the corps command and I as its commander -- we provide as precise information as possible to our subordinate units about the strength, the composition, and disposition and the objectives of the actions of the terrorist forces in the territory of Malo Kosovo, Drenica, Malisevo, and Salja, as well as Bajgora. To be quite specific, or rather, even more accurately than was done by the 3rd Army commander, we define and describe in even greater detail the enemy forces that the corps will have to handle, so to speak, that the corps would have to deal with.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Fair enough. General, I would now like us to move on to page 3, that's paragraph 2, task of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... The general answers, I believe the part of his answer in page 16, line 16 and 17, has not been recorded. He said that the corps will have to handle -- that the corps will have to deal with in case it happens. I believe it can be clarified, either by witness or by audiotape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is there any need for me to revisit this with the witness or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't think so, Mr. Bakrac. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with you. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, could you please look at paragraph 2, task of the Pristina Corps, and could you please read this sentence.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the permission of the Trial Chamber, I would like to say that paragraph 2 in accordance with the rules of combat is copied from the order of the superior command. Whatever the army commander set as a task for the corps, the corps command is not entitled -- does not have the right to make any changes. And it is stated here that the corps with the reinforcements that are enumerated here and with the armed non-Siptar population in Kosovo and Metohija will carry out an attack in the zone in accordance with the map. The task is in coordination with the forces of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia to block, rout, and destroy the Siptar terrorist forces in the general sector of Malo Kosovo, Drenica, and Malisevo, and at the same time they were to defend the state border and the various axes in Kosovo and Metohija to cut a long story short.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, what I would like to know, General, is whether you issued -- you said that it says here the armed non-Siptar population. Did you issue any specific tasks to any specific units in any of your orders? I mean a unit, a formation, of the armed non-Siptar population, was any specific task ever given with the exact designation of the unit?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the permission of the honourable Trial Chamber, I would like us to look at paragraph 5, and I will begin my answer as we wait for it to appear on our screens. Because the army commander did not specify, did not define in detail those forces, the civil defence detachments or local guards in specific locations in his order, what I did is in paragraph 5 where I as the commander regulate the tasks that are to be issued to the subordinate units, I didn't give any such tasks to my brigades. So I didn't issue any task to any of my brigades regarding the use of the armed non-Siptar population, as was the term that was used in this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General -- well, we have paragraph 5 here on our screens, tasks of the units. You gave us an explanation. But I wanted us to go back to something that precedes paragraph 5, the preceding paragraph talks about readiness. Could you please explain to us what were the provisions for readiness.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is a very important part of the corps commander's decision, which is again based on the decision of the army commander. For the first tasks, the tasks to secure and defend the state border and to secure the military facilities in the corps area, the readiness is stated as immediate. So units have already been engaged in those tasks and they have to continue. So there is no discontinuation. The only thing that may happen is that these forces are reinforced. Now, as for that specific task that was given, breaking up the strongholds of the terrorist forces in those three locations, this was to be stipulated in a special order and the code was Munja, lightning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what does it mean D plus four -- three to four days, that is once the signal, Munja, lightning, was received?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was not known when the signal would be received, the signal word lightning, or special order was to be issued. But I think that we will find the specific answer to this question at one point. I don't know whether the Trial Chamber would allow me to point out that in paragraph 5 all the corps units from the first tactical groups down to all the brigades, you will see that none of the brigades was issued any tasks for the use of the civil defence and civilian protection units which are termed in -- both in my order and in the order issued by the 3rd Army commander the non -- the armed non-Siptar population.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, we don't have to go item by item because I am sure that Mr. Hannis will bring up anything that you did not mention, so we can move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please just look at page 12 of this same order dated the 16th of February. Just --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you please just look at paragraph 10.3, or rather, the third paragraph from above, third paragraph down from the beginning of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please just scroll the document up a little bit. I do apologise. In English that would be page 27 down at the bottom of the page, so to assist the Trial Chamber. No, no, that's the next page, 28, in English. And then the next one, 29. That's page 29 -- no, page 30, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, during the execution or during the conducting of combat operations, can you read us -- for us that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "During the conducting of combat operations, expressly prohibit the uncontrolled entry of unit members into populated areas, looting of property of the local population, violations of the provisions of the international law of war, the displacement of weapons and military equipment belonging to the enemy of bodies, and entry into enemy shelters prior to the arrival of specialist organs."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see page 14 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can we comment item 10.7.1 which is technical support.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this item, in keeping with the rules of combat, units are define the expenditure of ammunition in combat sets for the execution of specific missions, and it can be seen that the approved use of small arms ammunition is two combat sets and for the heavier or, so to speak, for the artillery it is from 0.5 to one combat set. And for tanks, which is actually the ammunition were combat vehicles, 0.5 combat sets is the quantity which is allowed, meaning that in the execution of this task we expect to clash with the strongest armed rebellion forces, but the use of ammunition ordered is very restrictive. And I should like to ask the Trial Chamber to clarify the meaning of the concept of combat set because we will be encountering this later. And the best way to do it is on the basis of the first dash, the combat set for a rifle is the number of bullets that a soldier carries on himself, meaning that a combat set per soldier is 150 bullets or rounds. If two combat sets are allowed, that means 300 bullets for the execution of the tasking in question has been approved per soldier. As regards weaponry, each piece of artillery weaponry or tanks has a certain number of shells or projectiles from 12, 16, 30, to 42.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And, General, are there any rules or any norms that define the number of combat sets that is allowed or customary? I'm no expert on the matter, so would you kindly explain.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a special military science, separate branch and doctrine, which regulates -- in detail, prescribes in detail the ammunition to be used for the destruction of specific targets, depending whether they are fortified or not, and the planned expenditure of ammunition or lethal assets. But I shall stop on this particular occasion at this. There will be more occasion to explain this in more detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. Let us revert to our basic topic. Would you please now take a look at item 10.7.6, that is at page 15 in the B/C/S version. In the English it is 39. Can you read item 4 and explain it for our benefit.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did I understand you well, 10.7.6 is the item you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an item dealing with logistical support. All prisoners which defines that all detainees should be taken to what is referred to as the collection point of -- points for prisoners of war, and after having been questioned by the authorised competent organs of the MUP -- of the military security, they should be handed over to MUP organs for further processing. That is normally the substance of international conventions defining the treatment of captured persons or prisoners taken during combat activities. Having said this, I should like to add on this occasion as well that throughout the war in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija and in the zone of the corps, although this is prescribed by combat rules there was not set up a single collection point for prisoners of war but they were evacuated outside the zone of the combat -- of combat operations in order to save them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, we shall be coming to that, General. There is a document which deals with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, on this question of prisoners of war, can you give us an idea of the numbers of prisoners that were taken between the -- say the middle of February and the middle of June and shipped out, as you say, to other areas?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the combat reports of the Pristina Corps command, I recall a number of 215 captured members of the armed rebellion forces that -- who were taken prisoners primarily in defending the state border, who were handed over to the organs of the Ministry of the Interior. But right now I'm not speaking about the number that was taken prisoner by the forces of the Ministry of the Interior. And by your leave, I should like to say that I know that the total number, including 1998 and 1999, was over 1500 captured and arrested members of the terrorist forces who were released from prison in the year 2000. Although final sentences had been rendered in regular trials in respect of most of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So is the provision that we're looking at here related to the question whether you may have taken NATO prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Distinguished Bench, this refers to all of them. As far as I can recall, there were three NATO members who had been taken prisoner during the armed conflicts. Some were on the boundary between the zones of the Pristina and the Nis Corps, and they were also evacuated outside the zone of combat. And shortly thereafter they were released.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- During Jackson's mission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm trying to understand the concept of a prisoner taken in combat. I understand that you might want to prosecute KLA activists as terrorists or for the various crimes they committed, but was there a category of prisoner of war that applied to KLA combatants?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the 24th of March, 1999, when the state of war was declared, the category of prisoners of war also referred to KLA members and there were captured KLA members that were tried by military courts. And we have heard here from one witness, I believe, who was not exactly knowledgeable, but I do have reliable information -- perhaps some evidence shall be led to that effect that there were prisoners of war who were KLA members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And it's the number of those that I was asking you about. How many KLA prisoners of war were taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By the Pristina Corps, 215 as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I thought you had qualified that and said that these were taken by the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. What I said was this -- I do not include in this number because I don't know how many were taken prisoner by the forces of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I now I understand. I think I misread the answer. Why were the 215 handed to the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this point, Your Honour, I have two explanations. First, the Pristina Corps couldn't - and we shall see also that the 3rd Army could not under conditions of such heavy aerial bombing and from a distance, too - it could not set up camps and collection points for prisoners of war because in particular in the area of Kosovo and Metohija it was absolutely insecure, and I would say that it would have been inhumane, we just had no conditions, no possibility to create such collection points. That is on the one hand. On the other, a number of the KLA members who were taken prisoner at -- in a specific area, normally with arms and in uniform and in combat, but where there were no difficult consequences for the members of the army with prior so-called security processing they would be handed over to the Ministry of the Interior. The gravest cases, those who directly endangered the lives of army members or killed army members, were retained, were kept, and were put on trial before military courts rather than civilian ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will try to -- this is a voluminous material and we are proceeding gradually and have sought to systemize our subject matter. There is evidence that it was requested that a collection centre for prisoners of war be set up, there is evidence to that effect, and perhaps we shall be able to locate it during the break and present it to you while this topic is still on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I just want the transcript to accurately reflect what you said. You said they were handed over to the MUP, and as I understood you MUP then handed them over where, to whom?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I could gather and as far as I know, they handed them over for further processing to the civilian judiciary system.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, we have gone a bit away from our basic topic, and let us wrap up this document. Please look at item 11, commanding and support -- and communications, sorry, and can we have your comment and that is the last page in last item --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you move on, what you're saying is you may have information about the names of the 215 prisoners and we'll be able to trace their fate through the system? Is that what you're hoping to give us?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. There is evidence the Pristina Corps and the 3rd Army did not have a prison for war prisoners. That is the evidence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, they passed them to the MUP and the MUP passed them to the civilian authorities is what we've just heard from Mr. Lazarevic, but do you envisage being able to provide the records to show what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the sixth Defence will be probably able to do that. I don't know who is in question. What I asked Mr. Lazarevic was whether he knew what the MUP did then with the prisoners, what was the further procedure with the persons who had been handed over to the MUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Item 11, command and communications, regulates who will and from what place command if this order is to be realised, the command post of the corps in peacetime and the rear command post in Gracanica and the forward command post in Pristina in the Film city area. This is the regular, the usual customary way of doing this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Please explain this particular sentence. I believe that you commented on it yesterday. You have the sentence which begins with a plan.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The plan of communication coordination with the air force and anti-aircraft defence and the MUP forces should be regulated through a communications order. This means that another component, another structure which is not within the system of subordination with the corps, such as the aircraft defence, anti-aircraft defence and MUP forces, and the air forces of the Yugoslav Army are, then coordination or communications plan is drafted through which coordinated action with these components is actually carried out. All this is defined in a special order which is called order for communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, we shall now move on. You also saw reference to a special signal in it. Did the command of the 3rd Army issue directly before the war any order or an order that could be perceived as such, in that sense?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall that on the day an imminent threat of war was declared, the 23rd of March, 1999, the army command issued a special order - when I say "special," one can understand it as an executive order - for the beginning of the defence of the integrity of the state of the territory of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have in e-court 5D1294.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Please take a look at the document and tell us whether this is the one you've just referred to and could you comment on it, please.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the order issued by the commander of the 3rd Army in which he orders that in case air-strikes begin on any part of the territory of the FRY all the units engaged in the previous plans, according to the previous orders, are to be activated for the defence of the does he go to of the country in order to prevent the infiltration of NATO forces and the aggression by terrorist forces from Albania and Macedonia with ground forces or -- I don't see the following items, but probably the engagement of corps forces to break up the terrorist forces in the depth of the area of responsibility of the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, that's in item 1.6. And now we can move on and look at another document before the break. General, are you aware - and I will call for a Prosecution document, P1990 - that the Ministry of the Interior also planned for the conflict, or rather, for participating in the defence of the territory for terrorist forces?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that when the corps command drafted the order to neutralise the terrorist forces in those three major locations, the organs -- the operative organs of the corps command achieved coordination with the people dealing with planning in the MUP in order to have coordination and coordinated action. I didn't see the plan, but I know for certain that there was coordination.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please now scroll down.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It says here that the staff was planning three actions in Podujevo, Dragobilje and Drenica. Is this what you were just referring to?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, mopping up the terrorists in the Podujevo, Dragobilje, Drenica areas. These are the locations: Lap, Drenica, Malisevo, Dragobilje, those are the three locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, that was about to be my next question. Now, are these the three locations mentioned in your order of the 16th of July [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, those are those three locations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It may be I'm misunderstanding something here, Mr. Lazarevic, but you said that the operative organs of the corps command achieved coordination with the people dealing with planning in the MUP in order to have coordination and coordinated action. I did not see the plan." Is that not something you would normally see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Possibly it's a misinterpretation. I wish to remind Your Honours that the initial order of the army commander and my order was that in cooperation with MUP forces, the task of breaking up the armed rebellion forces on three location was to be carried out. Following that task, the operative organs in the corps command dealing with planning, I remember well, contacted the people, the individuals dealing with planning in the MUP, but the order issued by the MUP organs is something I did not see. I -- that's what I was referring to when I said I didn't see that document, but I know that there was coordination in preparation for the carrying out of this task.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would there not be a document which reflected the coordination?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that is a very good question. Yesterday or the day before I said that apart from the item in which the order that there should be coordination is issued, it was left up to the lower levels of command to implement that cooperation. As you saw in the previous document, through an order for communication, coordination is achieved and the rules of combat say that special cooperation plans have to be drawn up; however, such special cooperation plans were not drafted. Instead, what was drafted was something replacing such a coordination plan, and we will see it very soon and that really is a problem that you have in understanding certain documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we get too far along, at page 28, line 11, it says 16th of July. I thought we were talking about February.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish to thank my learned friend. I was about to intervene. My colleague is right, my learned friend is right, I asked about the 16th of February, whereas it says the 16th of July in the transcript. I think that now is a convenient moment for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. We shall resume at five minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, I wish to ask for your leave to complete the picture and make it completely clear. The first order from January issued by the General Staff is something I only mentioned for the record, but in order to have a full picture of everything we have been talking about, it might be a good idea for the General to comment on it. So we will now ask for 3D690 on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, this is a directive issued by the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia dated the 16th of January, 1999. MR. BAKRAC; [Interpretation] Please let's look at page 4 in B/C/S and it's page 8 in English. It's page 4 in B/C/S and page 8 in English. English page 8, B/C/S page 4, and it's item 3, tasks. It's page 5 in English. I do apologise. Yes, now we have both the B/C/S and the English versions on the screen. And where it says tasks and under 3.1 it says 3rd Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you comment on that, please.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the directive issued by the Chief of the General Staff in this item specific tasks are issued to the 3rd Army according to stages, there's the first stage and the second stage. In the first stage taking measures to protect from air-strikes by NATO forces, prevent introduction of a NATO brigade from Macedonia into the area of Kosovo and Metohija. At the same time, close off all the axes making it possible for terrorist forces to act from Macedonia and Albania, make sure that roads are passable primarily in the Pristina Corps area --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Read all this in the way you suggested before. We're familiar enough now with the theme as you've explained it, so it's not necessary for Mr. Lazarevic to read all this to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The first and the second stage were in coordination with the forces of the air force and the -- air force defence where terrorist forces are to be prevented from coming in from Albania, was this later translated into an order to the Pristina Corps as we saw a little while ago.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the principle. As a corps commander, I cannot alter the task given to me by the army commander, so yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We've been over all this, Mr. Bakrac. Please let's move ahead. There's a limit to how much you need to spell out to us about chains of command and how they work.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, we'll move on. The plan that had been drafted previously for the engagement of units in combat, your plan of the 16th of February, 1999, did it automatically enter into force or were some other activities undertaken in the Pristina Corps command?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's nothing automatic in the implementation of tasks of this importance in the defence of the country. There have to be ever more specific orders for specific parts of the plan. I recall that a day or two before a state of war was declared there was specific planning in the corps command pertaining to how the task of the 16th of February would be implemented, and there it said according to a separate plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 5D276 up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It appears to be your document and could you please comment on it. General, you have in front of you this document. Could you please comment on it.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document from the Pristina Corps command dated the 22nd of March, 1999. This is my concept in my capacity as the corps commander. This is how on the basis of the order of the 3rd Army commander, based on the Grom 3 directive and his special decision, how to conceive the destruction of the terrorist forces in those three locations. And assessing the overall -- the current situation of the manning level of the corps, I suggested to the army -- 3rd Army commander not to implement this task in full but only in part because the corps did not have enough forces, and it is -- it can be seen from this document that I propose that the terrorist forces be neutralised only in Donja Drenica, not in the whole area of Drenica, as the plan envisaged; not in the whole of Lab, but only in the upper part of Lab; and the Malisevo location was left out completely. The procedure now was as follows: I presented this concept of mine to the 3rd Army commander. He was at the command post of the Pristina Corps at the time. I was also presented to his operations officers, and only once he verifies this concept of mine or amends it, then a specific order is drafted for the execution of a combat task.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: If we look at page 2, the last sentence, could you please comment on it. It says here a request was sent to the MUP for the use of engagement of their forces and coordination was -- a coordinated action has been organized with them.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now we come to the specific explanation of the previous question. In the planning of counter-insurgency and counter-terrorist activities, the corps command had coordinated actions with the MUP forces in their turn in their own plans they envisaged the neutralisation of terrorists in these locations. And I notified the army commander that this coordination had been achieved.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, please. Your Honour, there's some kind of a conflict between the transcript and the document. The transcript says with regard to the last sentence in the document that a request was sent to the MUP for the use of engagement of their forces. The document, on the other hand, says MUP submitted a request to have their forces engaged. I don't know which one of those is the right translation of the -- of the actual situation, whether the request was made to MUP or MUP made the request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ackerman. Mr. Lazarevic, can you clarify that, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly. We saw from the previous document that MUP planned in parallel independently from the 3rd Army command and the corps command --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's not as complicated as that, Mr. Lazarevic. Just tell us who made the request. Was it the VJ or the MUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says here that MUP submitted a request for the coordination of coordinated action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you allow me now that we're talking about this document. In the heading of this document it says "concept," and this word is missing from the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, we will now call up an exhibit that you've already seen here, and I would like you to comment on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 5 -- P1966, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When we were talking about the previous document, you spoke about upper Lab and lower Drenica. Is the Malo Kosovo area related to any of these locations?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Upper Lab is part of Malo Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, we've seen this document a few times and we will be commenting on the addendum to the decision. Could you please explain to us who drafted this document and what is this document all about.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since the 3rd Army commander accepted my concept or my proposal for the implementation of the combat task, the operational organs at the corps command started the planning process for the implementation of this task. In light of the previous experience from 1998 in the planning of the coordinated actions with the MUP forces or support to the MUP forces, the operations officers in the corps command in the heading of this memo, they wrote the Joint Command for KiM and they recorded this document in the log-book of the Pristina Corps, and this order for the routing and destruction of the terrorist forces only in the Malo Kosovo area, so not in all the three locations, this order was then sent to the corps units for the purpose of the execution of the combat task.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The tasks were then issued only to the Pristina Corps units; is that so?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and you can see that in item 5 on one of the pages of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please first look at item 4, decision, that's on page 2 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Just before item 5 it says: "Readiness for the routing and destruction of STS," and then there is a blank day, blank hour. Can you please explain that.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time when this document was drafted, it was impossible to determine with any accuracy the time when the task was to be executed. That is why the readiness is not specified. This is not an executive act, an executive document. It was impossible to act on it because readiness was not defined. As such, it is a kind of a preparatory order for a forthcoming task.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You mentioned item 5. I don't think that we have to go through all of it, but could you just tell us briefly the units -- unit tasks, could you tell us something about the tasks that were envisaged for these units. Item 5 begins on this page and then continues on to the next page.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In item 5, as far as I can remember, a task was issued to combat groups of individual brigades. I don't know whether there were four or six of them in total, and their task was in coordination with the MUP forces to actually implement this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You say in coordination -- in a coordinated action with the MUP forces. How was this coordinated action between MUP and the army, how was it actually done?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This coordination was done at several levels. The first level was the corps command, and let me tell you right away that there was also the army command at the corps command with the organs from the MUP staff that deal with the planning of forces for combat. And I would like to add that the MUP staff in Pristina was not alone. There were some deputies or assistants to the minister of the interior who also participated in that. The coordination was also done at the level of the brigade commanders and the level of the MUP detachments or the secretariats of the interior. Through the exchange of information about the engagement, the execution of the task, the communications, agreements about liaison officers to be posted, and planning that at a certain place and at a certain time the representatives of the police and the army would come together to the combined post, combined command post that we were talking about where they would command and control their respective forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, could we now move to the addendum to this decision, that is P1967 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you do that I have a number of questions to try to clarify the situation here. Mr. Lazarevic, what's the relationship between this document and the previous one, that was your proposal or your concept?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this document stems from the concept since the army commander agreed with my concept or proposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've told us that there are efforts, presumably through meetings or other communications, at various levels to arrange coordination. What about at your level, who did you meet in the MUP to arrange to coordinate your activities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I personally as the corps commander did not have any coordinated actions with anyone. I did not call anyone for consultations or discussions or preparations. This was done by the operations officers in the corps command, and their opposite numbers in the MUP, in the police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What about the commander of the 3rd Army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 3rd Army commander was at the Pristina Corps command post in Pristina by that time in its peacetime location, and to my knowledge at that time he did not have any particular communication at that time because in 1998 the coordination system, the system of coordination between the army and the MUP, was already well in place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This document that we're looking at came from the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija. What was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that's the question that we've been trying to find an answer to all this time. This is a document from the Pristina Corps command for the combined execution of the tasks with the MUP forces. The title of the document in the heading is not appropriate. I state that quite categorically. It is not in accordance with the rules of combat. As I explained yesterday, the term "combined command" and "combined command post" are used in the rules of combat. This term was first used in 1998, and the operations officers, both in the 3rd Army and in the Pristina Corps, continued to use this term which, Your Honour, refers only to situations where coordinated action had to be carried out with the MUP forces. It was not used in any other situation. And the purpose of this term was to suggest to the subordinate units that this task was to be carried out in coordinated action with MUP or by supporting the MUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I see the last page of this document, please, on the screen. Mr. Lazarevic, you'll see the final words of this document, that: "The Joint Command shall command and direct all forces during combat operations from the Pristina area," then it's signed Joint Command for Kosovo. So who's in command of this series of combat operations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this document refers to a specific operation, one action, and item 13 regulates coordinated action and what you have read out is written in the last sentence of this item, and that mean what I sought to explain over the last two days, namely, that there would be combined commanding of the army and police. The term "combined" was replaced by the term "joint," i.e., Joint Command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You see, the Joint Command is a singular expression and it applies to all forces during combat operations. And what we would like to do is identify what this Joint Command is. I, for one, don't understand what you're actually saying to me at the moment, I have to confess. If you can help me understand it, fine, but I don't at the moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I fully appreciate why it is that you fail to comprehend what I'm saying. I shall try once again, but please do bear with me and try to remember what I explained yesterday when I talked about combined commanding. Namely, combat rules --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I understand what you were trying to say yesterday, Mr. Lazarevic, but can I take it that you approved of this use of the expression "Joint Command"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This term, joint command of the army and the police in the execution of combat tasks, was already in use in the course of 1998 and is still being used now. But please, when you look at this document, it exclusively speaks about the tasks of the Pristina Corps units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So does the last sentence: "The Joint Command for Kosovo shall command and direct all forces," apply only to the Pristina Corps forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. It refers to the Pristina Corps forces; but using this clumsy designation it also indicates that MUP shall have its own command, detachment command, that shall command its own forces, and that is this combined commanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: With the greatest of respect to you, Mr. Lazarevic, and applying basic common sense, it does exactly the opposite because the previous sentence to that makes it clear that the -- the job is to organize coordinated action with MUP forces and to introduce the concept of a Joint Command seems to me to cause confusion or state the very opposite of what paragraph 13 so far has said. So that's why I don't understand what you're saying. However, perhaps, Mr. Bakrac -- it's important that you understand that I don't understand, and Mr. Bakrac, perhaps, can endeavour to clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps the following documents shall help clarify matters. Before we deal with this question of the combined command post can we take a look at the supplemental decision P1967.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And would you please comment on it and then we shall move on. This amendment to the decision, the heading of which is again joint KiM command, refers to the previous order for -- related to Malo Kosovo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The previous order with -- which does not specify the readiness, so according to the previous order which did not specify the level of readiness, they could not proceed with the execution of the task. So this is an abridged order which is called a decision. It has the same heading, it has a number, a subnumber, which is related to the previous document, but this document now defines the actual time of the execution of the task concretely. And we should see page 2 in order to see the further course.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The task units -- the unit tasks are on the second page, but the readiness is indicated on this page, right, it is at 6.00 on the 24th of March?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that it is so and now I see that it is so. Readiness to break-up and destroy Siptar terrorist forces at 600 hours on the 24th of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now move to page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Here the specific tasks of all the units are indicated; am I right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the concrete tasks for the -- of the units to support the MUP forces in the execution of this specific task.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Concrete tasks for your units, right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now move to the very last page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, the KM in the region of the village of Lausa, what does that stand for?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command post shall be in the sector of the village of Lausa during the execution of this task, and that is by a combat group of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And at the bottom, can you see to whom this document was sent?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was sent to the 15th Armoured Brigade, to the 125th, to the tactical group 211, and to the 354th Infantry Brigade comprised within the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Had it been sent to anyone else, would that have had to be indicated here?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Was the previous document, 1966, in fact signed by you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The previous document, Your Honour, is not signed, and all -- such documents are without signature except for this one which is currently on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, these are the copies we have, but what about the original at the time the document P1966 was issued, was it signed by you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I did not sign a single one, Your Honour, except for this one document which is on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And why is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because such documents with such a heading, which I must say is inappropriate, which replace both the coordination plan and order were not signed by anyone in either 1998 or 1999 because such documents were to serve to subordinated brigades as guidance documents; and in addition to these documents they also received other documents with a heading of the corps command and signed by the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Excuse me for saying that I'm further confused, and this needs to be clarified. You made a proposal or concept on the 22nd of March which we saw, and there was then the Joint Command document of the 22nd of March. Your proposal or concept had been accepted. Is there a document from the 3rd Army commander accepting your concept?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There exists such documents, Your Honour. I don't know specifically about this activity, but it is enough for the army commander to sign the map. However, the corps command was also inclined to opt for these concepts of ideas given in this way, in written form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, let me ask the question a different way. When the commander of the 3rd Army approved your concept, how did he do it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He heard my proposal. With the proposal I also carried a map, and he actually approved my concept on the map itself. And sometimes he would write a couple of sentences stating, I approve your concept, proceed with the execution of the task. But please understand that the army commander was physically present with me throughout this entire procedure. We were in the same room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Following that, you issued -- or let me start that again. Following that, there was created P1966, the 22nd of March document, which you say is -- was unsigned in its original form. Who was that issued to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Pristina Corps command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What do you mean by the Pristina Corps command? You're issuing the document as the commander of the Pristina Corps, as I understand it. So when it goes to the Pristina Corps command, who do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I say "the Pristina Corps command," I mean the entire command, the commander, the organs which draft the specific documents. The documents that we are discussing now are drafted completely by the operations organ of the Pristina Corps command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did this document have a map attached to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As a rule, each of these documents would have a decision map attached and these -- but on these decision maps it was not written "Joint Command," but "decision of the commander of the Pristina Corps."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Was there such a map attached to this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In respect of this action I cannot be a hundred per cent sure because I do not have the document available, but, Your Honour, I hope that in the further course of these proceedings we will have occasion to see such documents, such maps which accompanied this type of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If there was no such map, how would anyone receiving P1966 be able to determine that it was authentic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These documents, as well as all other documents, would be delivered by official mail to the subordinated command in -- under specific cover or in a specific envelope in which the sender's address would be indicated; or the liaison officer from the corps command would, as courier, physically take it; or the commander of the brigade would come to the corps command to receive these and a series of other documents; or, fourthly -- and fourthly, there would be preparations executed for the realisation of this task. And the commander of the brigade would easily realise what this was. He knew exactly what it was, to whom it referred, what kinds of documents these were, and what he was to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I take it from all that you've said that if we are looking at documents in 1998 and 1999 which bear on the face of them to be from the Joint Command for Kosovo but are not signed, there's every likelihood that they are authentic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these documents are, from the aspect of the command of the Pristina Corps, are authentic. They were created where I have indicated, they were filed in the log of the command, and they were sent to the units of the Pristina Corps. And I assure you that the commanders who received those documents could come and say what these documents were and what they meant for them, including the other documents that were attached to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You've explained exactly to whom this was addressed. Please just tell us now, in the army is it possible to amend the decision issued by a higher command, a superior command, or is it practically impossible?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An amendment to a decision can only refer to one's own document or a document issued by a subordinate command. A document issued by a superior command may not be amended or modified in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have in e-court 5D463.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, this is a daily combat report issued by the command of the 125th Motorised Brigade. It's not long. It can be read all the way to item 5, but please read and comment on item 5, activities of the units.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a combat report issued by the 125th Brigade which participated with some of its forces in the execution of the task we are talking about. In item 5.1, the combat group, combat group 1, has been engaged pursuant to a decision by the Pristina Corps commander to destroy the terrorist areas in the area of Donja Drenica. In item 5.1.4, combat group 4, I'm reading the last sentence, is participating in coordinated action to destroy the terrorist forces in the area of Bajgora and Malo Kosovo. The brigade commander, therefore, however clumsy that document may look to us, understood that it was a decision issued by the command of the Pristina Corps, and he acted on it. He is here informing me that he is acting on my decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have Exhibit 5D1357 on the screen. It's a combat report of the corps command to the 3rd Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you comment on it, please. What is this about, with special reference to item 4, please.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a combat report of the corps command of the 25th of March addressed to the 3rd Army command. I can't see item 4 very well. If you're referring to situation in the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm reporting to the army commander that in the course of the day combat operations were conducted to break-up and destroy terrorist forces in the general areas of Orahovac, Podujevo, and Drenica.
