utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have 5D1358, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Item 5 on page -- well, before that. The date is the 26th of March, 1999, and it's a combat report of the Pristina Corps command to the 3rd Army?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let's look at page 2, item 5, activities and situation in the units.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the combat report of the Pristina Corps command I inform the army commander that according to the plan of the Pristina Corps command, the units in combat groups are successfully implementing the tasks to destroy terrorist forces in the Drenica area. Pursuant to the decision and plan of the corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And the next page, item 8. Do you see here that the focus of activities for the following day and so on?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The focus of activities for the following day, if you look at the fourth line, is breaking up and destroying terrorist forces in accordance with the Pristina Corps command plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have P1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, this is an analysis of the activities of the 549th Motorised Brigade, and I would like us to comment on page 2. Let's turn to page 2. On page 2 above where it says conclusion, that's the last paragraph, but three paragraphs above that could you please read slowly so the interpreters can follow.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Command of the envisaged forces was unified -- was combined --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- "through joint" --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that your translation differs from the Serbian version which is why I asked the General to read this slowly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, he had better read it again because he wasn't allowed to complete it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was not interpreted.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you read slowly from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Command of the envisaged forces was combined by the Joint Command of the forces of the MUP and the Army of Yugoslavia."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That seems to come to the same thing, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a problem with translating the word "objedinjeno." Could we say by the combined Joint Command [In English] MUP and VJ.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter suggests that this be referred to CLSS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Each of the translations suggested so far comes to the same thing. There's a Joint Command of the MUP and the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We'll now go back to some other activities of yours in the course of February, before the beginning of the aggression. In some situations, did the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia ask for specific reports on certain events; and if it did, why?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, there were several situations where the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia asked the corps command directly to deliver a separate report on certain events in the corps area. I can only speculate as to why.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, let's look at 5D251.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did you accept that it was within the authority of the Chief of the General Staff to ask for a direct report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, and as the subordinate commander in the 3rd Army I was duty-bound to inform him that I had received such a task, and this was not unusual and there was nothing odd about it. And a report could be sought directly from the corps. The date is the 23rd of February, 1999 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just let me complete the questions I have. Would the Chief of the General Staff have authority to give you direct orders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The superior has the right to issue a certain order to the second level of subordination, but if he does not inform the first subordinate, that is, me, I am duty-bound to inform my first superior of such an order. So, yes, he does have that right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There may be a translation problem with this answer. You said the superior has the right to issue a certain order to the second level of subordination. Now, you would be the second level of subordination; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you comment on this document and why this was sought?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 20th of February, 1999, there was a large-scale attack in the general area of Suva Reka by terrorist forces on part of the 549th Motorised Brigade, which was engaged in reconnaissance of the area for the dislocation of material reserves. The OSCE mission was there when the attack took place. The attack went on for a few hours. I informed the command of the 3rd Army in my regular daily report. As far as I can recall, the liaison team or the signals team of the 3rd Army, the liaison team of the OSCE mission also sent a report to the General Staff about this; however, it's possible if I may be allowed to make assumptions a little bit, bearing in mind that we have seen some documents from the collegium of the Chief of the General Staff where there was some ideas about such events and some thoughts about them, whether the Chief of the General Staff decided directly to ask for confirmation of these events by asking for a report from the corps commander -- well, maybe yes. And this is my report wherein the first item, I inform him that nothing happened in Vucitrn. The army did not engage in any activities. I then go on to explain what happened concerning the attack in Suva Reka. And in item 3 an incident that had taken place between the OSCE mission and the unit that was in the border belt, where that unit did not permit the OSCE mission to enter without the liaison officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Why do you think a direct report was sought?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, at that time I did not know that; but as I sit here, I now make this assumption by your leave on the basis of what we've heard and the evidence that we've seen about the meetings of the collegium of the Chief of the General Staff where some members of the collegium gave their own interpretations of the developments in the corps area of responsibility, explaining that they obtained this information from some other sources. And the Chief of the General Staff then went to the corps commander for confirmation to get the first-hand information. But this is what I'm speculating now on the basis of what I saw in some of those documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sounds rather convoluted, Mr. Lazarevic. Are you saying that you think the Chief of the General Staff maybe suspected he wasn't getting the whole story, or am I reading too much into your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would rather be inclined to say that he had some information that did not tally with what is written here in this text, but let me assure you, I know that information of this nature was contained in other documents, quite specifically in the documents from the liaison team with the OSCE mission in the 3rd Army, about these very same events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What measures did the Pristina Corps command take in order to carry out the tasks it had received, given the conditions and given that it had its peacetime forces?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were measures that pertained to the implementation of the tasks received from the General Staff via the 3rd Army command, but with the application of certain work methods by specifically defining the implementation of those tasks in periods briefer than seven days and through written orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In order to maintain and improve the combat-readiness, did you have any meetings with your subordinate commanders or did you have any collegium meetings before the combat operations actually started?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The corps command in this period when it was not war, or peace, decided to work directly with the subordinate commands -- commanders in the form of briefings at the corps command. All of them were there to analyse the security situation and the combat-readiness in units. At those meetings, specific tasks were defined that applied to a period of time shorter than seven days.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, lest we should go into all of the documents that contain those tasks, let me just for the record note the exhibits -- Defence exhibits that we will -- that we're referring to, that's 5D252, 5D260, 5D272.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: -- Did you ever at those briefings and at those collegium meetings with your subordinate commanders plan any activities targeting the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not. And I hope that once the Trial Chamber has inspected those documents, the orders that pertain to the very beginning of the war and the period immediately before the war, will see that these documents regulate the improvement of the combat-readiness in strictly peacetime conditions, documents that specify key tasks, and there is not a single word about what you were asking me about, about any plans that might refer to any crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, in light of the seriousness of the situation on the eve of the NATO air-strikes, did you issue any orders instructing the military personnel, restricting the movement of army personnel in uniform outside of the barracks, or anything of the sort? Or let's just look at Exhibit 5D277, it appears to be your document. Could you please comment on it.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is order, this is my order, an order by the corps commander. It was signed by the Chief of Staff because I was probably not present there, warning the subordinate commanders on the day before the imminent threat of war was declared that because of the increased terrorist attacks that have grown more frequent, measures should be taken that active-duty personnel and the corps personnel in public places should not go out, should not appear in public, in uniform, which in a way, if somebody were to look at it from outside, it is humiliating. You're ordering your subordinates not to wear uniforms, but the gist of this warning, the gist of this order, is that the appearing of corps personnel in uniform might cause the conflicts to escalate, might cause further attacks on the army and the violence could spiral out of control even sooner.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We see that in item 3 you insist on full discipline.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in virtually every order - and I hope that I will have the opportunity to go through some other orders - but in this order disciplined performance or carrying out of this order and other orders is something that is insisted on and reports are sought on the execution of those tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would now like to move on to a different topic, so perhaps this might be a convenient time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we can break now and we'll resume at five minute to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, we've seen and heard here that the OSCE mission on the 20th of March, on the eve of the bombing left Kosovo and Metohija. Can you tell us as the corps commander whether the KLA exploited this situation in the field; and if yes, in what way?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this was a dramatic time on the eve of the aggression. The attacks by the rebel and terrorist forces throughout Kosovo and Metohija doubled in intensity. These attacks targeted the military, the police, and the civilians. I remember quite clearly, in particular in the Drenica area in Metohija, and as far as I can recall now in just four days after the withdrawal of the OSCE mission there would be 15 to 20 attacks daily, on the average. Around 15 persons were killed and over 30 people were injured in those four days. The storm was looming on the horizon and it was quite clear that the war would break out. This could be seen from those terrorist activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did the KLA - and there is some operational intelligence and some combat reports - use the M-77 uniforms of the Army of Yugoslavia; and if yes, how was that possible?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not operational intelligence. This was a widespread practice. Terrorist groups wore the army uniforms and the army insignia. They did not wear just the M-77 uniforms which are older, but also M-89 uniforms. There were numerous reports from the units that sustained such attacks, and as far as I can remember as the corps commander I personally issued warnings. I remember that the General Staff and the army commander warned about this phenomenon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And how was it possible, sir, that those uniforms were used?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the problem -- it is not a big problem to procure a military uniform or a uniform resembling a military uniform. I remember that in January 1999, the military district command, it is subordinate to the 3rd Army, gave us information that there were over 5.000 military uniforms, that the former military conscripts of Albanian ethnic background failed to return to the army. So this was one source of such uniforms. We heard in this courtroom evidence from Prosecution witnesses that they had military uniforms in their possession. Also, in various markets it was possible to obtain those uniforms in illegal ways. So this was not such a big problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to refer the Trial Chamber to 5D184 and 5D947. We would proceed more quickly if we would now not open each and every document dealing with those issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: As the NATO air-strikes began, were just some parts of the Kosovo and Metohija territory targeted by the KLA, the attacks on the authorities, state institutions, and so on?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The whole of the territory of Kosovo and Metohija was affected by the armed rebellion. I would say that there was not a single village, a single town, a single settlement where there were no attacks on the institutions of the state, the security forces, civilians, primarily non-Albanians, but also on Albanians who did not join those paramilitaries formations of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you in the corps have information that NATO forces were planning a ground attack, first on Kosovo and Metohija and then on the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We in the corps command received intelligence from the 3rd Army and directly from the General Staff, but we also had our own intelligence and operational information. And it was our very, very considered assessment that there was a great certainty that there would be such a ground aggression by NATO forces on the area of responsibility of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Were there reports - I mean your operational reports - that established a link between the start of the NATO attack and the large-scale movement of the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were operational reports and intelligence reports, but there was also the situation on the ground, right from the first day of the aggression against the country, that was the 24th, and even perhaps a day before when it became quite clear that there would be the aggression against the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have on our screens Exhibit 5D692.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: This is information number 113. It is a telegram sent by the chief of the intelligence information, General Krga, and in item 2 on page 1, the last paragraph just before item 3, the last paragraph in item 2, I would like you to comment on this paragraph and I will be asking you some questions related to the military doctrine in this context.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This intelligence report from the General Staff indicates that the General Staff has intelligence, that NATO air force had targeted the Siptar facilities and refugees in order to force them to leave the territory of Kosovo and Metohija in as large numbers as possible, in order for NATO to be able to fire on the security forces in Kosovo and Metohija as indiscriminately as possible. And as quoted here, "to prevent the Army of Yugoslavia from using the civilians as human shields."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, let us leave aside intelligence report. What I want to know. You said that you are a career military officer, that you've been -- that you were a military officer for 32 years. In military tactical sense, in the sense of the military doctrine, was it reasonable to move out the civilian population and to expose one's own forces to NATO air-strikes without, as is said in this intelligence report, any reserves in terms of the ability to target civilians?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the sense of military doctrine, this would be extremely risky. It would be extremely unacceptable and dangerous, but I want to tell the Trial Chamber that the corps command, together with the army command, discussed this issue in light of the threats that we had received through the foreign media, from NATO officials and statesmen, from some countries that Kosovo and Metohija would be turned to dust, and that as many civilians as possible would move out. And the army commander, as far as I can recall, phoned the General Staff to see whether something could be done through the state authorities from the standpoint of humanitarian concerns to prevent the moving out of the civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Where was the focus of NATO attacks in Kosovo and Metohija? What did they target primarily?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The focus of NATO's air campaign and remote strikes was the border area towards Macedonia and Albania, over 250-kilometre front, which was between 20 and 25 kilometres deep, where they had daily isolating of the battle-field, as it was referred to. This was exceptionally heavy shelling and strikes with every conceivable, available, lethal asset of this greatest, biggest world military group.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 5D1336 shown on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you -- this is a map, this exhibit is a map, and could you please comment on it. You say, General, in the -- the objective was isolating the battle-field. Can you clarify this military term for us, and there are many of us who are not quite sure what that means, are not familiar with such terms.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Isolating the battle-field means that on the area in question everything which is found there is destroyed and neutralised without discrimination as regards objectives. This is -- this involves military and civilian objectives, everything which stands in the way of a land intervention -- of the land intervention that was being prepared from the areas of Albania and Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you now take a look at this map and explain to us. It seems that all the NATO aviation attacks are located there, but they are also blue and rectangles and triangles, can you tell us what this is about.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an overview map of the shelling by NATO forces in Kosovo and Metohija. According to the reports of the Pristina Corps and the 3rd Army, there were over 2.000 aerial strikes on the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, with 37 per cent of the strikes targeting civilian facilities, civilian targets, and the red triangles mark civilian targets and the blue ones the military and police or, in a word, military targets. Normally you could not have drawn in 2.000 attacks or strikes in this map, and not even that figure is quite accurate. At the command post of the 3rd Army there was a special group of officers, including officers from the air force corps, and they maintained these figures as precisely as they could.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I just want to put something on the record. This does not appear to be on my list of exhibits in the notification. It's the second one today. It may not be a big issue, but if I got it in a supplemental notification, I'd like to be informed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It may, indeed, be a big issue, Mr. Hannis. The suggestion is 37 per cent of air-strikes targeted civilian facilities. Now, you -- it's difficult to tell that from the -- in fact, you can't tell it from the map, but it may be a prelude to some detailed information about what these 700 or so facilities were.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, for exhibits that I wasn't given notification of, then I would insist on a little more foundation as to what this is because it's the first moment I'm seeing it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, can we lay a foundation for this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I omitted to inform my learned colleague, Mr. Hannis, and we received an explanation of this document a while ago from the -- from General Lazarevic, namely, that the group at the command post, the forward command post, maintained records as far as it could according to the information it gathered and the combat reports, the sites and localities of NATO strikes. But let me say at the outset or in advance, rather, we do not have precise figures about these 600-plus civilian facilities. We can obtain them a bit later, subsequently. There does exist a white paper on it, I believe. My colleague Visnjic knows more about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, let me just add that I announced this document in my schedule for the cross-examination so that there should be no problem for the Prosecution, and of course I do not object to colleague Bakrac using it in his examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I still think it would help, Mr. Bakrac, if we discovered how this was compiled and who compiled it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know that, Your Honours. We can ask the General if he knows it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, you heard a question of Their Honours, of the -- His Honour. Who actually compiled this, do you know what the origin of this document is?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know quite reliably. I have seen a document numbering tens of pages which was generated at the forward command post of the 3rd Army during the war, which includes all military and civilian targets throughout the territory of the 3rd Army that were targeted by NATO aviation strikes and remote shelling. This overview which is not quite clear on the right-hand side, this rectangle actually indicates exactly the towns and the municipalities, the targets in these towns and municipalities, how many civilians, troops were targeted, et cetera. So that is the basis upon which this map was created. I don't know whether that document which is quite voluminous has very many pages is in the case file, but if it is necessary, and if so instructed by the Trial Chamber, I personally know how that document can be obtained quite quickly -- relatively quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, in connection with this map, as the corps commander were you aware of NATO's use of banned ammunition, radioactive ammunition, and cluster bombs in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware of that, I was aware of that as the corps commander, and so was every member of the corps. And unfortunately, also numerous civilians, namely, that NATO had used everything it had apart from a classical nuclear bomb, but radioactive ammunition, yes, and to a very large extent too.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: As the corps commander, in fact, that you were aware of this fact, did you take any measures?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I should like to say to the distinguished Chamber that already in mid-March appraising the situation and this -- assessing this very certain use of these terrifying weapons, we ordered that special ABH units should be prepared, units of the atomic, biologic, chemical defence --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would counsel please not overlap with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up 5D268, which is the relevant order and then you can continue talking about the measures taken and why they were taken.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a document of the corps command signed by the Chief of Staff of the corps, and this is information which was received from the General Staff which was being passed on to all units along with instructions as to how to proceed if radioactive ammunition is used, but you stopped me in midsentence. I wanted to say that we in the corps, on the basis of this document but also on the basis of our own evaluation and appraisal, we decided already before the war to form a reconnaissance and observation elements of atomic, biological, and chemical defence units which would following each air-strike reconnoitre the locations that were targeted, that were struck, effect dosimetric control of the location, mark the location, warn both civilians, the civilian population, as well as the security forces not to approach the area and, if possible -- possible for the location to be decontaminated, and I should like to say that tens of scores of locations were controlled and inspections under air-strikes involving private facilities, socially owned facilities, and military facilities which were controlled for radioactive radiation following the strikes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, we heard General Petkovic's testimony here. He was the chief of the ABH defence, and there was something controversial. I believe that the Presiding Judge also asked him whether there was any data about the use of cluster bombs and other bombs in the period end March and beginning of April. Do you know whether cluster bombs were used already at the end of March and beginning of April?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd like to say this. I personally know that -- because at the end of March the general area of the corps command post and several adjacent villages were targeted by a large number of cluster shells which we defused in order to prevent the civilian population and troops from getting hurt.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have Prosecution Exhibit P2297 up on the screen, and this is the war log of the 52nd Battalion of the military police. The date is the 31st of March, 1999. The page number is K05208757 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: But the interpreter is not quite sure of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is page 3 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Until we get the English version, look at the 31st of March and read the first page out for us. Was this what you meant when you said that you were personally aware of that happening and that it was in the command zone?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the period I referred to, and I specifically spoke about this region, about this sector. On the 31st of March, during the night, the position of combat vehicles was targeted in the lower part of the Kisnica village where a cluster bomb fell, there were no consequences. Let me tell you, a cluster bomb contains 450 banned cluster bomblets in it, of which one-third or even 50 per cent remain active for ten years or even more, and if activated by anybody via a sensor, the consequences are disastrous. That was in the immediate vicinity of the command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, at the very beginning of the war, were there also civilian targets hit by NATO strikes?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately from the very outset of the air campaign, of the bombing campaign, a large number of targets in both rural and particularly in urban communities, such as Pristina, Djakovica, Prizren, Urosevac, and let me not enumerate them all.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have Exhibit 5D980 up on the screen, and until it is shown on the screen, I should like to say that this is a regular combat report of the command of the military district dated the 5th of April, 1999, addressed to the command of the 3rd Army at the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Please comment on item 1, the first paragraph, or rather, the second paragraph and the third paragraph -- and the third paragraph.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The targeted area was the military district of Gnjilane, the village of Koretiste, and the Binacka Morava factory, Kosovska Mitrovica, the mining facility of Stari Trg, and the bridges and tunnels on the section of the road Gazivode-Ribarice, and the military district of Pristina, the monastery of Gracanica, the depot or war reserves of the command of the military district, that is a military target, the Jugopetrol storage, that's a civilian facility, and the Kosavski Junaci barracks. In the Pec military district they repeat, at the Gubavac hill was targeted and the military district of Prizren, the suburban settlements in Pec, Suva Reka, and Dragas. And of the larger towns and settlements in Kosovo and Metohija -- actually, from the larger towns and settlements in Kosovo and Metohija, there was continued moving out of the population, the Siptars were moving towards Macedonia and the Serbian population towards Nis and other towns.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So we can see from this combat report that it says there is continued moving out of both the Albanian and the Serbian population; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true. Everybody fled every which way wherever they could.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What was the procedure, or rather, did the Pristina Corps take any measures in order to render assistance when NATO strikes also targeted civilian targets?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the permission of the Trial Chamber, I should like to say this, under conditions when we didn't even know how many soldiers had been killed and where, all the corps units exerted maximum efforts in earnest in order to help the civilian population after every strike and after every such calamity, starting with the urgent -- the most urgent rendition of assistance to the survivors, their evacuation to military medical facilities or to civilian medical facilities. And to make a long story short, all conceivable measures including blood donations. I personally ordered my commanders to cease all other activities, and with special forces that had been structured beforehand join in the rendition of assistance to the -- all those who were the victims of such strikes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, are there combat reports that reflect that action?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Distinguished Presiding Judge, there do exist numerous reports, especially of brigade commands and the corps command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But are there no -- this is a combat report of whom? This is -- this is from the Pristina Corps, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, distinguished Presiding Judge, this is a combat report of the military district of Pristina to the command of the 3rd Army on the 5th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So what you say is there will be other combat reports which do actually indicate the sort of action being taken that you've just described? Obviously it wasn't required in this case, but there will be other examples; is that the position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, there were such reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was just about to assist. We'll come to a part of my cross-examination where we shall see -- of my examination-in-chief where we shall see what the Pristina Corps undertook and what steps it took to look after civilians, but we were trying to take things step by step and show all the possible reasons why the civilian population left the province, and this can be seen from some combat reports. We'll come very soon to these reports and the specific measures taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, what was the overall task of the Pristina Corps and were there any priority tasks?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Pristina Corps in wartime found itself at the strategic focus of the defence of the country at a front stretching over 250 kilometres with the general task of defending the integrity of the country from aggression. The priority tasks within that overall task were the following: Protecting manpower, material resources from air-strikes and from attacks by the armed rebels; prevention of further penetration of the aggression forces into the territory of Kosovo and Metohija; thirdly, efficient combat control of the territory, which was to make it possible for the other subjects of defence to efficiently become included in the defence of the country; the fourth priority task was successive mobilisational and operative deployment for the implementation of this task.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: How were the corps forces engaged and in what echelons? Was there a plan in March and April?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The forces of the Pristina Corps, both according to the Grom 3 plan, that is, the peacetime forces, were concentrated and focused on defending the state border. Just before the beginning of the war and with the beginning of wartime operations special orders arrived for the strengthening of those forces, and in early April there was another complex plan for the defensive operation carried out by the corps known as Grom 4. This plan was basically the central plan throughout the 78-day war.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: That is a plan issued by the command of the Pristina Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the plan I've been talking about. Such a plan existed at the level of the 3rd Army and also at the level of the General Staff, but this time it was the Pristina Corps command that first drafted the plan; after that, it was the 3rd Army and the General Staff because this was a priority.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that's 5D175.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An order of the command of the Pristina Corps for defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And now let's look at the first page, after that the third page, item 2, tasks of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order of the corps commander for defence, it's a state secret, Grom 4 and in the first item the aggressor forces are described, as are their intentions, goals, and possibly method of action.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Now, please look at item 2, the tasks of the Pristina Corps and comment on that very quickly.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This task, as I've already explained, was copied from the order issued by the 3rd Army commander, and the gist of it is that in coordinated action with the MUP forces and the forces of defence, further penetration of the aggression forces into Kosovo and Metohija were to be -- was to be prevented. So the aggressor forces had to be stopped at any cost, and then with the additional engagement -- with additional engagement, these aggressor forces were to be expelled from the territory of FRY. And in this passage, the one before the last, the armed non-Siptar population is mentioned again, and that's the part that did not alter from the previous order. A command post is designated in the Kisnica area, and this was immediately -- not just the command post, but the entire village was subjected to attacks with cluster bombs.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Now, please look at item 4.1, third paragraph.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the paragraph beginning with: "With part of the forces ..."?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, and please comment why this says so.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in this item my decision refers to the defence of the country in the corps area, and the paragraph in question says: "With part of the forces secure the territory and prevent a spillover of terrorist forces from the Pecinje district Montenegro and the Raska-Polinlje district into the Pristina Corps area of responsibility." This implies that the corps is not only an 251-long-kilometre front facing Macedonia and Albania protecting the country and not only is it neutralising the armed rebellion within the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, but it also must prevent on the right and left flank the spillover of terrorist wing, the spillover of terrorist forces from Pecinje district and other places.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now let's look at 217 on page 14 -- 12.7 on page 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The last sentence before this.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. In all the combat documents of any nature, including the most general and basic war plan, this is a plan for the defence of the country, there is an order, there is a decision. In all situations consistently respect all the provisions of the international laws of war and, let me add, a large number of special orders were issued almost every other day as to how the provisions and rules of conduct should be applied, both of humanitarian law and the international law of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, we'll come to all those special decisions, but, General, item 13, command and communication, that's on page 15. Yes, we see that corps command post has been provided for, also a forward command post. Can you comment on this?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The command post of the corps in the area of the village of Kisnica, that's an abandoned mine. Then there is a rear command post in Gracanica and a forward command post that was still not operating. There was a command group in Djakovica, but very soon it would become a forward command post when the chief of the corps went to head this group. That's why there is a blank space here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, let's look at the last page. It seems that in this plan, Grom 3, coordinated action with the air force, the anti-air defence, and the MUP forces has been provided for and envisioned?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me correct you. This is not Grom 3. This is Grom 4, but you are right. Coordinated action with the air force and the anti-aircraft defence on the territory of Kosovo and Metohija and with MUP forces is regulated in the order for communications. And with Their Honours' leave, because the Presiding Judge asked me a question as to whether this coordinated action was regulated anywhere, let me say that this order for communications is an integral part of this entire order, as are a number of other orders, and I think it even has an exhibit number. But all I want to do is point out that this large -- this capital N refers to the order for communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, in the indictment there is mention of forces of the FRY and Serbia --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see my colleague Mr. Zecevic on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Page 71, 14, I believe the witness says order for communication which defined the -- which defined this or something along these lines. Maybe witness can be asked again to verify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, you may wish to clarify this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You heard my colleague. Can you clarify, Witness?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was going to confirm once again that with the order for communications, the communications of coordinated action are concretely being regulated with the air force, anti-air force defence, and MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. I will repeat my previous question. In the indictment there is mention of the forces of the FRY and Serbia. Can you tell us what defence forces were engaged in Kosovo and Metohija in 1999, when the war started?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will risk generalizing the Law on Defence and the actual situation on the ground, and I will mention the three main structures of forces in the defence system which were engaged during the war on the territory of Kosovo and Metohija. These were the forces of the Army of Yugoslavia, the forces of the Ministry of the Interior Affairs of the Republic of Serbia, and the forces of the Federal Ministry of Defence of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. So I'm not speaking of any other forces or subjects of defence here, and in accordance with the Law on Defence, citizens, organizations, and organs, federal, republican, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: As for the Army of Yugoslavia now allow me to reformulate my question. Who organized, prepared, and commanded the units of the civil defence and civilian protection?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The preparation, organization, training, equipping, and use of the forces of the civil defence and civilian protection on the territory of Kosovo and Metohija was carried out by the competent organs of the Ministry of Defence of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and these competent authorities were the following: The administration for defence in Pristina and the regional organs of that administration within the districts and municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Who commanded these forces during the war?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These forces were commanded from the top of the Ministry of Defence through the administration for defence of the Republic of Serbia and then down the chain, which I mentioned the administration of defence in Pristina, and then the regional or district ministries of defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Would you be so kind as to comment a Prosecution exhibit, P1339.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could it be placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You referred just now to the administration for defence of the Republic of Serbia. What is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, within the civil defence as an institution at the level of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and within the scope of the Ministry of Defence, there are two administrations at the level of the member republics. There is an administration for defence at the level of the Republic of Serbia and another administration for defence at the level of the Republic of Montenegro. May I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's sufficient. Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, could you please look at this exhibit. Does it show that the civil defence, or rather, could you please read paragraph 1 and comment on it.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By Your Honour's leave, the very stamp of this memorandum, the heading, the letterhead, to be more specific in answer to your previous question, the federal ministry of defence, the district organ in the Republic of Serbia, this is what it says there, this is this organ at the level of the Republic of Serbia, and this organ issues orders to the administrations for defence in the territory of Serbia. In paragraph 1 it is -- it says: "I hereby order that all organizational units of the Federal Ministry of Defence, district organ for the Republic of Serbia, to receive orders exclusively from the seat of the district organ for the performance of all the duties and tasks in the area of the defence of the country." This is signed by the head of this organ, Colonel Manastirac, later General Manastirac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does that mean that this organ is part of the Government of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid, Your Honour, that I cannot be very specific here. I'd rather say that this was a part of the ministry of the defence of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, but it has a detached administration, both at the level of the Republic of Serbia and on the level of the Republic of Montenegro, as can be seen from this stamp here where you have the Federal Ministry of Defence and the district organ in the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know the strength of the civil defence?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must admit that as the corps commander, I really didn't have any relevant data about this particular body. To tell you the truth, Your Honour, apart from knowing one of the chiefs in Pristina, I was not aware of their structure, of their organization. On the basis of the documents that I've seen in the course of this trial, I've been able to ascertain that their establishment strength was over 9.000, and recently I've been able to see a document originating from the Ministry of Defence indicating that their strength was even greater than that. So I really don't know how many people they engaged during the war, how many people they mobilised and armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we are not referring to the exhibit number now. We will be using it in the course of our case. This was not announced to the Prosecution. It has not been translated yet. We will be using it later, and the exhibit number is 5D1368. This is a document speaking about the strength of the civil defence. I see that it's one minute to 7.00. By courtesy of my colleague Mr. Ackerman I, received information that the list of prisoners, of captives, has been admitted into evidence as an exhibit, the number is 4D509, it is an exhibit of Mr. Pavkovic's Defence, and perhaps now this would be a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's not admitted into evidence, it's just in e-court, but it's the list that you were inquiring about earlier, a list of prisoners.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. We shall then adjourn now and resume at 11.00 tomorrow in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
